name: mean2
title: Fast averaging over subset of vector elements

origin.description: Computes the sample mean of all or a subset of values.
origin.usage: mean2(x, idxs = NULL, na.rm = FALSE, refine = TRUE, ...)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: refine
arguments.text: If TRUE and x is numeric, then extra effort is used to calculate the average with greater numerical precision, otherwise not.

origin.details: mean2(x, idxs) gives equivalent results as mean(x[idxs]), but is faster and more memory efficient since it avoids the actual subsetting which requires copying of elements and garbage collection thereof. If x is numeric and refine = TRUE, then a two-pass scan is used to calculate the average. The first scan calculates the total sum and divides by the number of (non-missing) values. In the second scan, this average is refined by adding the residuals towards the first average. mean() uses this approach. mean2(..., refine = FALSE) is almost twice as fast as mean2(..., refine = TRUE).
origin.example:
x <- 1:10
n <- length(x)

idxs <- seq(from = 1, to = n, by = 2)
s1 <- mean(x[idxs])                     # 25
s2 <- mean2(x, idxs = idxs)             # 25
stopifnot(identical(s1, s2))

idxs <- seq(from = n, to = 1, by = -2)
s1 <- mean(x[idxs])                     # 25
s2 <- mean2(x, idxs = idxs)             # 25
stopifnot(identical(s1, s2))

s1 <- mean(x)                           # 55
s2 <- mean2(x)                          # 55
stopifnot(identical(s1, s2))

translation.description: Computes the sample mean of all or a subset of values.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric or logical vector. Integer missing values are None. Double missing values are nan. Logical values are averaged as 0 and 1.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: 1-based positions to include, as in R. None selects every element. Zeros are dropped. Negative values exclude those positions. Missing and out-of-range positions contribute a missing value. This is idxs in R.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values are excluded. This is na.rm in R.

arguments.name: refine
arguments.text: If True and x is double, a second pass adds the mean of the residuals from the first average. Integer and logical data use one pass. The default is True.

translation.details: mean2(x, idxs) gives the same result as averaging the selected elements, without building that subset. The average is computed in the Rust crate mean2. For double data and refine=True, the first pass sums and divides by the number of non-missing values, and the second pass adds the mean residual. Index rules follow matrixStats validateIndices, with out-of-range positions allowed.
translation.value: A Python float. An empty mean is nan.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.mean2 import mean2

x = np.arange(1, 11)
n = len(x)
idxs = np.arange(1, n + 1, 2)
s2 = mean2(x, idxs=idxs)         # 5.5
idxs = np.arange(n, 0, -2)
s2 = mean2(x, idxs=idxs)         # 5.5
s2 = mean2(x)                    # 5.5
